questions.q: Diimide for the reduction of an alkene is most simply generated in situ from:
options: Hydrazine and KOH at high temperature
questions.explain: H₂O₂ oxidises N₂H₄ to HN=NH and water. Hydrazine with KOH and heat is the Wolff–Kishner reagent for C=O, not a diimide source.

questions.q: 1,2-Dimethylcyclohexene is reduced with diimide (N₂H₄/H₂O₂). The product is:
options: A 1 : 1 mixture of cis and trans isomers
questions.explain: cis-Diimide transfers both hydrogens to the same face of the C=C through a six-membered cyclic transition state (syn addition), so the two methyls end up cis.

questions.q: Which group is generally NOT reduced by diimide?
questions.explain: Diimide reduces non-polar C=C and C≡C bonds; polar multiple bonds such as C=O, C≡N and NO₂ are left alone.

questions.q: But-2-yne is treated with excess diimide. The product isolated is:
questions.explain: The cis-alkene formed first reacts almost as fast as it forms, so two HN=NH are consumed and butane results; to stop at the alkene, Lindlar catalyst is used.
